C2-1-0.title: Perfecto simple vs. continuo: ¿resultado o actividad?

items.note: La primera: terminado, mira el resultado. La segunda: actividad reciente, quizá sin acabar; explica la pintura en tu ropa.

items.a: She's **lived** in Medellín all her life.
items.b: She's **been living** in Medellín since the divorce.
items.note: Situación permanente vs. temporal: el continuo sugiere que no es definitivo.
Hábito neutro vs. queja: continuo + always/forever expresa irritación.
Conclusión ya tomada vs. proceso abierto: el continuo suena más tentativo.

branches.if: El resultado o una cantidad (cuántos, cuántas veces)
branches.example: I've **written** three chapters this week.

branches.if: La duración o la actividad en sí
branches.example: I've **been writing** all morning.

branches.if: Una evidencia visible de algo reciente
branches.example: Your eyes are red. **Have you been crying**?
I've **known** her since we were six.

steps.label: Pasado simple
steps.sentence: I **lived** abroad for ten years.
steps.change: Etapa cerrada: ya no vivo allí.

steps.label: Present perfect
steps.sentence: I**'ve lived** abroad for ten years.
steps.change: Sigue siendo verdad hoy; énfasis en el hecho.

steps.label: Present perfect continuous
steps.sentence: I**'ve been living** abroad for ten years.
steps.change: Énfasis en la experiencia en curso, quizá provisional.

steps.label: Past perfect continuous
steps.sentence: I**'d been living** abroad for ten years when I finally felt at home.
steps.change: Duración hasta un momento del pasado.

steps.label: Future perfect continuous
steps.sentence: By June, I**'ll have been living** abroad for ten years.
steps.change: Duración proyectada hasta un punto futuro.

C2-1-1.title: Del más directo al más tentativo

items.example: Can you check my draft?
I wonder if you could check my draft.
I wondered if you could check my draft.

items.word: I was wondering if you could…
items.example: I was wondering if you could check my draft.

items.word: I was just wondering whether you might…
items.example: I was just wondering whether you might possibly check my draft.

items.note: El pasado no habla del pasado: suaviza la oferta (muy típico en atención al cliente).
El continuo pasado deja espacio para un “no” sin incomodar.
Past perfect: esperanza frustrada (no viniste).
Sugerencia indirecta: quita presión al interlocutor.

branches.example: Can you grab me a coffee?

branches.if: Con un colega o un desconocido
branches.use: I wondered if… / Did you want…?
branches.example: I **wondered** if you **had** a minute.

branches.if: Un favor grande o a un superior
branches.example: I **was wondering** if you **could** write me a reference.
I**'d hoped** we **might** settle this informally.

items.b: I**'m thinking** of moving back to Bogotá.
items.note: Opinión (estado) vs. considerar un plan (acción).
Carácter permanente vs. comportamiento puntual, ahora.
Entender vs. salir con alguien.
Cualidad vs. acción de probar.
Posesión vs. experiencia que se vive.

C2-1-2.title: ¿Puedo usar -ing con este verbo?
C2-1-2.question: ¿El verbo describe un estado o una acción con intención?

branches.if: Un estado, una opinión o una posesión
branches.example: I **feel** that the decision is unfair.
The vet **is weighing** the puppy.
I**'m realising** more and more how much I miss home.
I**'m loving** this new job.

steps.label: Estado
steps.sentence: This parcel **weighs** two kilos.

steps.label: Acción
steps.sentence: The clerk **is weighing** the parcel.

steps.label: Estado
steps.sentence: I **expect** they'll be late.

steps.label: Acción
steps.sentence: We**'re expecting** guests tonight.

steps.label: Estado
steps.sentence: You **are** so selfish.

steps.label: Comportamiento
steps.sentence: You**'re being** so selfish today.

steps.label: Neutral
steps.sentence: The minister leaked the report to the press on Monday.

steps.label: Foco: quién
steps.sentence: **It was the minister who** leaked the report.
steps.change: It-cleft: destaca (o corrige) a la persona.

steps.label: Foco: cuándo
steps.sentence: **It was on Monday that** the report was leaked.

steps.label: Foco: la acción
steps.sentence: **What the minister did was (to) leak** the report.
steps.change: Wh-cleft con do: destaca lo que hizo.

steps.label: Foco: el suceso
steps.sentence: **What happened was that** the minister leaked the report.
steps.change: Presenta toda la noticia como información nueva.

branches.if: Corregir un dato (no X, sino Y)
branches.example: **It wasn't the data that** was wrong; **it was the interpretation**.

branches.if: Crear expectativa antes de la idea clave
branches.example: **What really worries me is** the lack of evidence.
**All I asked for was** an apology.
**It wasn't until** I read the transcript **that** I understood.

items.a: **What I said was that** the plan was risky.
items.b: **It was the plan that** I said was risky.
items.note: La primera destaca el contenido de lo dicho; la segunda, cuál cosa (y no otra).
“All” añade “solo eso”, y a menudo suena a reproche.

items.a: **The reason why** he resigned **was that** he'd lost support.
items.b: **The reason why** he resigned **was because** he'd lost support.
items.note: La segunda es redundante (reason… because); en escritura formal se prefiere that.
En registro cuidado, el verbo concuerda con lo que sigue: is + singular, are + plural.

steps.label: Neutral
steps.sentence: The days when politicians admitted mistakes are gone.

steps.label: Participio al frente
steps.sentence: **Gone are the days when** politicians admitted mistakes.

steps.label: Neutral
steps.sentence: Her argument was so persuasive that the jury changed its mind.

steps.label: So + adjetivo al frente
steps.sentence: **So persuasive was her argument that** the jury changed its mind.

steps.label: Such al frente
steps.sentence: **Such was the outcry that** the bill was withdrawn.
steps.change: Such + be + sustantivo: el escándalo fue tal que…

items.note: Objeto al frente sin inversión: tono contundente, muy oral.

items.a: **Strange though it may seem**, I miss the old system.
items.b: **Though it may seem strange**, I miss the old system.
items.note: Adjetivo + though/as: concesión enfática y literaria.

items.a: **Into the chamber walked** the Prime Minister.
items.b: The Prime Minister walked into the chamber.
items.note: Lugar al frente + inversión con verbos de movimiento: efecto narrativo.
Con pronombre sujeto no hay inversión: la segunda es incorrecta.

C2-2-1.title: ¿Qué estructura de énfasis elijo?
C2-2-1.question: ¿Qué quieres destacar al principio de la frase?

branches.example: **So convincing was the speech that** few questioned it.
**Such was the backlash that** the advert was pulled.
**More alarming still was** the minister's silence.
**Try as she might**, she couldn't sway them.

C2-2-2.title: ¿Hay inversión o no?
C2-2-2.question: ¿La expresión negativa o restrictiva afecta a toda la oración?

branches.if: Sí: niega o limita la oración principal
branches.example: **At no time did** the spokesman deny the claim.

branches.if: No: es una expresión fija sin valor negativo
branches.example: **In no time**, the story went viral.
**Only when** the leak emerged **did they** apologise.
**Not until** the trial **did** the truth come out.

C2-2-2.title: No sooner / Hardly: una cosa justo después de otra

steps.label: Neutral
steps.sentence: As soon as the speech ended, the protests began.

steps.label: No sooner
steps.sentence: **No sooner had** the speech ended **than** the protests began.
steps.change: No sooner + had + sujeto + participio + than.

steps.label: Hardly / Scarcely
steps.sentence: **Hardly had** the speech ended **when** the protests began.
steps.change: Con hardly/scarcely va when, no than.

steps.label: Only once
steps.sentence: **Only once** the speech had ended **did** the protests begin.
steps.change: La inversión va en la oración principal.

items.example: Seldom does a slogan change anyone's mind.
Rarely have I heard such a feeble excuse.
Little did they know the tape was running.
Never has a lie travelled so fast.
Under no circumstances should sources be named.
She can't have seen us, or she'd have waved.
The witness might just be mistaken.
His memory could be playing tricks on him.
Early memories may well be reconstructed.
The results should be in by Friday.
You must have misheard me.

branches.example: He **must be** exhausted.
She **might be** pretending.
They **can't have** forgotten the date.

branches.use: may well / should / be bound to + infinitivo
branches.example: The tests **are bound to** reveal something.

items.note: Para la deducción negativa en pasado se usa can't/couldn't have; mustn't have suena extraño.
La primera es un reproche (no lo hiciste); la segunda, especulación sobre el pasado.
Well aumenta la probabilidad: “es muy posible que”.
El infinitivo perfecto lleva la especulación al pasado; el simple, al futuro.

items.b: I **didn't need to buy** a ticket.
items.note: La primera: lo compré y no hacía falta. La segunda: no era necesario (y normalmente no lo compré).
Should have: crítica directa. Might have: reproche irritado, muy británico.
Could: era posible (no pasó). Should: era lo esperable o lo justo (y no pasó).
Expectativa (probablemente ya llegaron) vs. plan fallido (no llegaron).

branches.example: You **needn't have cooked**; we'd already eaten.

branches.if: No era necesario (sin decir si se hizo)
branches.example: We **didn't need to queue**, so we went straight in.

branches.if: Lamentas o criticas lo que no se hizo
branches.example: I **should have trusted** my instincts.
We **could have taken** the train, but we drove.
You **might have told** me you were coming!

steps.label: Hecho
steps.sentence: I took an umbrella, but it didn't rain.

steps.label: Innecesario
steps.sentence: I **needn't have taken** an umbrella.
steps.change: Lo hice y no hacía falta.

steps.label: Hecho
steps.sentence: I didn't check the date, and I missed the deadline.

steps.label: Arrepentimiento
steps.sentence: I **should have checked** the date.

steps.label: Alternativa perdida
steps.sentence: I **could have asked** for an extension.
steps.change: Había otra opción que no usé.

branches.example: Someone's at the door. **That'll be** the courier.
**You'll have heard** the news by now.

branches.if: Un hábito típico (neutro o con cariño)
branches.example: On Sundays my grandfather **would take** us to the market.
She **will** leave her shoes on the stairs!
Well, he **would** say that, wouldn't he?

C2-3-2.title: Would vs. used to; will neutro vs. enfático

items.note: Would de hábito solo va con acciones repetidas, no con estados: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.b: He **WILL** sit there for hours, ignoring everyone!
items.note: Sin acento: comportamiento típico. Con acento: queja.
La segunda es una suposición segura, no un hecho comprobado.
Will añade el matiz de tendencia inevitable.

steps.label: Hecho
steps.sentence: The phone's ringing. It's my mother.

steps.label: Suposición presente
steps.sentence: The phone's ringing. **That'll be** my mother.
steps.change: Lo deduces por la hora o la costumbre.

steps.label: Suposición pasada
steps.sentence: She**'ll have seen** my message by now.
steps.change: Will have + participio: supones algo ya ocurrido.

steps.label: Hábito pasado
steps.sentence: Every evening she **would ring** at exactly seven.

steps.label: Verbal
steps.sentence: The firm **expanded** rapidly, so profits **fell**.

steps.label: Nominalizado
steps.sentence: The firm's **rapid expansion** led to **a fall in profits**.
steps.change: Las acciones se vuelven sustantivos; la causa pasa a un verbo de relación (led to).

steps.label: Verbal
steps.sentence: Staff were **unhappy** because managers **didn't consult** them.

steps.label: Nominalizado
steps.sentence: **Staff dissatisfaction** stemmed from **a lack of consultation**.
steps.change: Más compacto e impersonal: típico de un informe.

branches.example: **The implementation of** the policy was delayed.
They took ages to put the policy into practice.

branches.if: Quieres suavizar o no señalar a nadie
branches.example: **There has been a delay in** processing your claim.

branches.if: La frase acumula tres o más of
branches.use: vuelve a un verbo para aclarar
branches.example: We analysed **how cutting costs affected** morale.

steps.label: Relativa activa
steps.sentence: Applicants **who are applying** for the role must register.

steps.label: Reducida con -ing
steps.sentence: Applicants **applying** for the role must register.

steps.label: Relativa pasiva
steps.sentence: The candidates **who were shortlisted** will be contacted.

steps.label: Reducida con participio
steps.sentence: The candidates **shortlisted** will be contacted.

steps.label: Con infinitivo
steps.sentence: She was the first woman **to chair** the board.
steps.change: Tras first, last, only y superlativos.

C2-4-1.title: ¿Qué participio uso?
C2-4-1.question: ¿Qué relación hay entre las dos acciones?

branches.if: Ocurren a la vez, o la segunda es consecuencia
branches.example: **Working** late, she missed the call.

branches.if: Una ocurre antes y causa la otra
branches.example: **Having lost** the contract, they cut jobs.
**Faced with** bankruptcy, the firm sold its assets.
**Not having** the right degree, he was rejected.

items.a: **Walking** into the office, the smell of coffee hit me.
items.b: **Walking** into the office, I smelled coffee.
items.note: El sujeto implícito del participio debe ser el de la oración: el olor no camina.

items.b: **Having been promoted**, he saw his salary double.
items.note: Quien fue ascendido es él, no su salario.
El informe es publicado (pasivo): participio en -ed, no -ing.

items.a: **Given** the figures, a restructure is inevitable.
items.b: **Considering** the figures, a restructure is inevitable.
items.note: Given, considering y assuming funcionan como conectores fijos: correctos aunque no compartan sujeto.
Regret to: lamento comunicar (ahora, formal). Regret -ing: me arrepiento de algo pasado.
Mean + -ing = implicar. Mean to = tener la intención.

items.b: She **went on talking** for an hour.
items.note: Go on to: pasar a algo nuevo. Go on -ing: seguir con lo mismo.
Try -ing: probar como solución. Try to: esforzarse.
Propose to: tener la intención (formal). Propose -ing: sugerir.

C2-4-2.title: ¿-ing o to?
C2-4-2.question: ¿La acción del segundo verbo es anterior o posterior?

branches.example: I'll never forget **meeting** her.
Don't forget **to sign** the contract.
Promotion would mean **managing** twenty people.
We stopped **to review** the figures.

steps.label: Recuerdo
steps.sentence: I **remember signing** the contract.

steps.label: Tarea cumplida
steps.sentence: I **remembered to sign** the contract.
steps.change: Me acordé y luego lo firmé.

steps.label: Fin de una costumbre
steps.sentence: She **stopped working** weekends.

steps.label: Propósito
steps.sentence: She **stopped to answer** the phone.

steps.label: Pasiva implícita
steps.sentence: The proposal **needs revising**.

C2-5-0.title: Del rumor a la fórmula impersonal

steps.label: Activa
steps.sentence: People **say** that the algorithm is biased.

steps.label: It + pasiva
steps.sentence: **It is said that** the algorithm is biased.

steps.label: Personal
steps.sentence: The algorithm **is said to be** biased.

steps.label: Pasado anterior
steps.sentence: The data **is thought to have been leaked** in May.
steps.change: To have been + participio: ocurrió antes.

steps.label: En curso
steps.sentence: The firm **is believed to be developing** a rival model.

steps.label: Con there
steps.sentence: **There are reported to be** thousands of victims.

C2-5-0.title: ¿Qué infinitivo tras is said / is thought?
C2-5-0.question: ¿Cuándo ocurre lo que se dice respecto al momento en que se dice?

branches.example: She **is said to be** the brains behind the project.
They **are thought to be negotiating** a deal.
He **is believed to have fled** the country.

branches.if: Antes, y el sujeto recibió la acción
branches.example: The files **are alleged to have been destroyed**.

items.note: Activo: yo interrumpo. Pasivo: me interrumpen.

items.b: Patients expect **to be told** the truth.
items.note: Quién recibe la información lo cambia todo.

items.b: He denied **having been offered** a bribe.
items.note: Gerundio perfecto activo vs. pasivo.
Mismo significado; la estructura personal es más compacta y periodística.

C2-5-1.title: ¿Qué causativo?
C2-5-1.question: ¿Qué relación tienes con quien hace la acción?

branches.example: We're **having the server upgraded**.

branches.if: Lo mismo, más informal o con esfuerzo
branches.example: I finally **got my visa renewed**.
I'll **have my assistant send** you the file.
We **got the hospital to share** its data.

branches.if: Te pasa algo malo que no pediste
branches.example: She **had her account hacked**.

items.note: Causativo: lo hizo otra persona. Sin causativo: lo hice yo.
Have: instrucción normal. Get… to: tuve que convencerlo.
Para desgracias, have es lo natural; get sugiere que fue culpa suya.

items.a: I **won't have** you **speaking** to me like that.
items.b: I **won't let** you speak to me like that.
items.note: Won't have + objeto + -ing: no pienso tolerarlo (enfático, británico).

steps.label: Activa
steps.sentence: A specialist **is reviewing** our privacy policy.

steps.label: have + participio
steps.sentence: We**'re having** our privacy policy **reviewed**.

steps.label: have + persona + infinitivo
steps.sentence: We**'re having a specialist review** it.

steps.label: get + persona + to
steps.sentence: We **got a specialist to review** it for free.

steps.label: get + objeto + -ing
steps.sentence: The update **got the system running** again.
steps.change: Hacer que algo vuelva a funcionar.

C2-5-2.title: Del dato rotundo a la cautela

items.example: The study proves that screens cause anxiety.
The data shows a clear link.
The data indicates a link.
The findings suggest a possible link.
It would appear that the link is weaker than assumed.
It could be argued that the link is coincidental.

C2-5-2.title: Suavizar una afirmación paso a paso

steps.label: Rotunda
steps.sentence: AI **will replace** teachers.
steps.change: Demasiado absoluta para un texto académico.

steps.label: Modal + cuantificador
steps.sentence: AI **may** replace **some** teaching tasks.
steps.change: Se limita la certeza y el alcance.

steps.label: Verbo tentativo
steps.sentence: AI **appears to be** replacing some teaching tasks.

steps.label: Impersonal
steps.sentence: **It has been suggested that** AI may replace some teaching tasks.

steps.label: Adverbio
steps.sentence: AI will **arguably** reshape, rather than replace, teaching.
steps.change: Arguably: una opinión que se puede defender.

branches.use: may, might, could, be likely to
branches.example: These results **are likely to** vary across age groups.

branches.use: tend to, in most cases, to some extent
branches.example: Users **tend to** overestimate their privacy.

branches.use: It is argued / It could be argued that
branches.example: **It could be argued that** consent is never fully informed.
The evidence **points to** a gradual decline.

steps.label: Tercer condicional
steps.sentence: If we **had protected** the wetland, the floods **wouldn't have been** so bad.

steps.label: Mixto: pasado → presente
steps.sentence: If we **had protected** the wetland, the town **wouldn't be** underwater now.

steps.label: Mixto: presente → pasado
steps.sentence: If he **weren't** so short-sighted, he **would have backed** the plan.
steps.change: Un rasgo permanente explica algo pasado.

steps.label: Implícito
steps.sentence: **With more funding**, the project **would have succeeded**.
steps.change: La condición va en un sintagma, sin if.

C2-6-0.title: ¿Qué combinación?
C2-6-0.question: ¿Cuándo está la condición y cuándo el resultado?

branches.example: If they **hadn't cleared** the forest, the river **would be** cleaner.

branches.use: If + past simple, would have + participio
branches.example: If I **knew** more about birds, I **would have spotted** it.
I**'d have come**, but nobody told me.

branches.if: La condición está en un sustantivo
branches.example: **Without** bees, we **would lose** a third of our crops.

items.a: If I were you, I'd recycle it.
items.note: La condición va dentro de una expresión fija.

items.a: If anyone had seen the data, they'd have panicked.
items.note: La condición está en el sujeto: cualquiera que…

items.a: If you saw the reef now, you wouldn't recognise it.
items.note: El contexto basta: la condición queda implícita.

items.a: If we hadn't helped, they'd have failed.
items.note: Without + sustantivo sustituye a la cláusula con if.

steps.label: Primer condicional
steps.sentence: If you **should** notice any leaks, contact us.

steps.label: Should
steps.sentence: **Should you** notice any leaks, contact us.

steps.label: Segundo condicional
steps.sentence: If the government **were to** ban plastic, prices would rise.

steps.label: Were
steps.sentence: **Were the government to** ban plastic, prices would rise.

steps.label: Tercer condicional
steps.sentence: If we **had known** about the spill, we would have acted.

steps.label: Had
steps.sentence: **Had we known** about the spill, we would have acted.

items.a: **Had we not** intervened, the species would have vanished.
items.b: **Hadn't we** intervened, the species would have vanished.
items.note: En la inversión la negación no se contrae: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.a: **Were it not for** the wind farms, emissions would be higher.
items.b: **If it weren't for** the wind farms, emissions would be higher.
items.note: Misma idea; la inversión es más formal.

items.a: **Should** you **wish** to object, write to us.
items.b: **Should** you **to wish** to object, write to us.
items.note: Should + sujeto + infinitivo sin to: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.a: **Were I** the minister, I'd ban it.
items.b: **Was I** the minister, I'd ban it.
items.note: Solo were admite la inversión; was, no.

branches.example: **Should** the river **rise**, residents will be evacuated.
**Were** we **to lose** the forest, the climate would suffer.
**Had** they **listened**, the lake would have survived.

branches.if: Algo que impide o permite el resultado
branches.use: Were it not for / Had it not been for
branches.example: **Had it not been for** the rangers, the fire would have spread.

branches.use: provided / as long as / on condition that
branches.example: You can camp here **provided** you leave no trace.
The species will vanish **unless** poaching stops.
**Supposing** the glacier melted, where would the water go?

branches.if: Lo que habría pasado sin algo
branches.example: **But for** the rain, the fire would have spread.
Close the gate; **otherwise**, the goats will get out.

C2-6-2.title: De la suposición a la condición estricta

items.example: Assuming the funding comes through, we'll start in May.
You can stay as long as you respect the rules.
Provided the data is accurate, the model works.
They signed on condition that the forest remained untouched.
Only if emissions fall will the reef recover.

items.a: Take a raincoat **in case** it rains.
items.note: In case: por si acaso (precaución previa). If: solo cuando llueva.
Casi equivalentes; unless destaca la única excepción.

items.a: **Even if** they pay us, we won't sell the land.
items.b: **If** they pay us, we'll sell the land.
items.note: Even if: la condición no cambia el resultado.

items.a: **But for** your help, we'd have failed.
items.b: **Except for** your help, we'd have failed.
items.note: But for = si no hubiera sido por. Except for = excepto: la segunda cambia el sentido.

branches.if: Una oración tras think, hope, expect, suppose
branches.example: Will the film win? I **expect so**. / I **hope not**.
I prefer the original version to the new **one**.
The critic was asked to retract, but refused to **do so**.

branches.if: Un verbo tras un auxiliar o modal
branches.example: She said she'd finish the novel, and she **has**.
I didn't want to go, but I had **to**.

items.note: La segunda es formal o enfática; en conversación se prefiere la primera.
Con hope la negación va con not: la segunda es incorrecta.
If so = si es así; if not = si no. Sustituyen una condición entera.

items.a: I haven't read it, but I **might do**.
items.b: I haven't read it, but I **might**.
items.note: Do tras un modal es británico e informal; ambas son correctas en el Reino Unido.

items.a: The painting? The **one** by the window.
items.b: The paintings? The **ones** by the window.
items.note: One y ones concuerdan en número; con incontables (music, advice) no se usa one.

steps.label: Completa
steps.sentence: Some critics loved the play, and other critics hated the play.

steps.label: Elipsis
steps.sentence: Some critics loved the play; **others** hated **it**.

steps.label: Completa
steps.sentence: He promised to review the book, but he hasn't reviewed the book.

steps.label: Elipsis
steps.sentence: He promised to review the book, but he **hasn't**.

steps.label: Completa
steps.sentence: Is the exhibition free? If the exhibition is free, I'll go.

steps.label: Sustitución
steps.sentence: Is the exhibition free? **If so**, I'll go.

branches.example: The plot was **extremely** clever.
The finale was **absolutely** breathtaking.
It was **really** good. / It was **really** superb.
The second act was **somewhat** predictable.

items.example: The film was slightly too long.
The acting was fairly good.
The book is quite interesting.
The ending was rather moving.
The script is extremely witty.
Her performance was quite extraordinary.

C2-7-2.title: Construir una frase nominal paso a paso

steps.label: Núcleo
steps.sentence: a **painting**

steps.label: + material
steps.sentence: an **oil** painting

steps.label: + origen
steps.sentence: a **Flemish** oil painting

steps.label: + época
steps.sentence: a **17th-century** Flemish oil painting

steps.label: + opinión
steps.sentence: a **stunning** 17th-century Flemish oil painting
steps.change: Opinión → tamaño → edad → forma → color → origen → material → propósito → sustantivo.

items.note: Delante del sustantivo lleva guion; después de be, normalmente no.
Con adverbios en -ly nunca se usa guion: la segunda es incorrecta.
En el compuesto, el sustantivo va en singular: la segunda es incorrecta.
Mismo sentido; el compuesto es más compacto y periodístico.

steps.label: Con should (británico)
steps.sentence: They insisted that he **should resign**.
steps.change: Should + infinitivo: alternativa frecuente en el Reino Unido.

steps.label: Subjuntivo
steps.sentence: They insisted that he **resign**.

steps.label: Negativo
steps.sentence: The court ordered that the names **not be** published.

steps.label: Pasivo
steps.sentence: It is essential that every vote **be** counted.

branches.if: Un verbo de exigencia o propuesta (demand, insist, recommend, propose)
branches.example: The union **demands that** the policy **be** withdrawn.

branches.if: Un adjetivo de necesidad (essential, vital, imperative, crucial)
branches.use: It is + adj. + that + verbo base
branches.example: **It is vital that** the inquiry **remain** independent.
**the requirement that** candidates **be** over 35
He **insisted that** he **was** innocent.

items.en: Far be it from me to…

branches.example: I **wish** the law **were** fairer.
**If only** we **had voted**.

branches.if: Una queja sobre la conducta de otro
branches.example: I **wish** politicians **would** stop lying.
**It's high time** the government **acted**.

branches.if: Una preferencia sobre lo que hace otro
branches.example: I**'d rather** you **didn't** post that.

items.a: He talks **as if** he **is** the boss.
items.b: He talks **as if** he **were** the boss.
items.note: Is: quizá lo sea. Were: no lo es (comparación irreal).

items.b: I**'d rather you stayed** at home.
items.note: Mismo sujeto: infinitivo. Otro sujeto: pasado.
Con el mismo sujeto no se usa would: la segunda es incorrecta.
Infinitivo: neutro. Sujeto + pasado: ya deberíamos haberlo hecho.

steps.label: Hecho presente
steps.sentence: The protest is banned.

steps.label: Deseo
steps.sentence: I **wish** the protest **weren't** banned.

steps.label: Hecho pasado
steps.sentence: We didn't speak up.

steps.label: Arrepentimiento
steps.sentence: **If only** we **had spoken** up.

steps.label: Urgencia
steps.sentence: **It's high time** we **spoke** up.

branches.example: **Much as** I admire her courage, I disagree with her tactics.

branches.use: despite / in spite of / notwithstanding / for all
branches.example: **Notwithstanding** the court's ruling, the protests continued.
The reform passed, **albeit** narrowly.
**However unpopular** it may be, the tax is necessary.
The evidence was weak. **Nonetheless**, he was convicted.

items.example: It was a good speech, though.
Even though they lost, they kept protesting.
Despite the ban, they marched.
Much as I sympathise, I can't agree.
a significant, albeit temporary, victory
The ruling notwithstanding, the law remains in force.

items.a: **Despite the fact that** he was innocent, he was jailed.
items.b: **Despite** he was innocent, he was jailed.
items.note: Despite no va con oración: necesita the fact that. La segunda es incorrecta.

items.b: The plan was effective, **albeit it was** costly.
items.note: Albeit va sin sujeto ni verbo: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.a: **However hard** they tried, they couldn't win.
items.b: **However** they tried hard, they couldn't win.
items.note: However + adjetivo/adverbio van juntos al principio.

items.a: **Strange as it may seem**, he won.
items.b: **As strange it may seem**, he won.
items.note: Adjetivo + as + sujeto + verbo; la segunda está mal ordenada.

branches.if: Un plan o intención (quizá no cumplida)
branches.example: I **was going to** run the marathon, but I got injured.

branches.if: Un destino que sí se cumplió (narración)
branches.example: She **was to become** the first Colombian woman to climb Everest.

branches.if: Un plan oficial que no se cumplió
branches.example: The race **was to have taken** place in May.

branches.use: was about to / was on the point of + -ing
branches.example: He **was about to** quit when his coach called.

branches.if: Un futuro visto desde el pasado
branches.example: Nobody knew that the injury **would** end his career.

C2-9-0.title: Mirar al futuro desde el pasado

steps.label: Presente → futuro
steps.sentence: The surgeon **will operate** tomorrow.

steps.label: Pasado → futuro
steps.sentence: The surgeon said she **would operate** the next day.

steps.label: Horario previsto
steps.sentence: The operation **was due to** start at nine.

steps.label: Inminencia
steps.sentence: The team **was on the point of** giving up.
steps.change: A punto de (más formal que about to).

steps.label: Destino
steps.sentence: It **was to be** his last match.
steps.change: El narrador lo sabe; el personaje, todavía no.

C2-9-0.title: Matices del futuro en el pasado

items.a: The match **was to be** played on Sunday.
items.b: The match **was to have been** played on Sunday.
items.note: La primera: estaba previsto (no dice si ocurrió). La segunda: estaba previsto, pero no ocurrió.
Intención (quizá olvidada) vs. justo en ese instante.
Las dos narran un futuro cumplido; was to suena más literario y fatídico.

items.a: We **were due to** land at six.
items.b: We **were supposed to** land at six.
items.note: Due to: horario oficial. Supposed to: expectativa, a menudo incumplida.

items.example: It's a tough sport. Mind you, serious injuries are rare.
To be fair, he did warn us.
That said, the risks remain.
Admittedly, the sample was small.
Conversely, inactive adults showed no change.
Hence the need for further trials.

C2-9-1.title: ¿Qué función necesitas?
C2-9-1.question: ¿Qué relación quieres marcar entre las ideas?

branches.example: **What is more**, the treatment is cheap.
**Admittedly**, the data is limited. **Even so**, the trend is clear.
Runners improved; **by contrast**, the control group did not.
Sleep was poor; **consequently**, performance fell.

branches.use: the former / the latter / this + sustantivo
branches.example: Both yoga and running help, but **the latter** carries more risk.

items.note: Mismo sentido; having said that es algo más oral.
Hence puede ir solo con un sustantivo; therefore necesita una oración completa.
On the other hand presenta otro aspecto; on the contrary niega lo anterior. No son intercambiables.
Incidentally = por cierto (cambio de tema). Accidentally = sin querer: la segunda no tiene sentido.

C2-9-2.title: Del phrasal verb al verbo formal

steps.label: Informal
steps.sentence: We **looked into** why patients **gave up** the treatment.

steps.label: Formal
steps.sentence: We **investigated** why patients **discontinued** the treatment.
steps.change: Verbos latinos de una sola palabra.

steps.label: Informal
steps.sentence: The team **came up with** a plan to **cut down on** risks.

steps.label: Formal
steps.sentence: The team **devised** a strategy to **reduce** risks.
steps.change: Más preciso y propio de un informe.

steps.label: Phrasal neutro
steps.sentence: The trial was **carried out** in 2024 and **set up** by the WHO.
steps.change: Algunos phrasal verbs son neutros y válidos en textos formales.

items.note: Result in = causa → efecto. Result from = efecto ← causa.
Comprise va sin of en registro cuidado.
With: una opinión o persona. To: aceptar una propuesta.

items.b: The kit **consists of** a mask and gloves.
items.note: Consist in = radica en (abstracto). Consist of = está formado por.
Attribute X to Y: la segunda es incorrecta.

branches.if: Informe, artículo científico o carta formal
branches.example: The meeting was **postponed** until further notice.

branches.if: Phrasal verb neutro sin equivalente natural
branches.use: se mantiene (carry out, set up, point out)
branches.example: The authors **point out** several limitations.
Doctors are still **looking into** the cause.

branches.use: verbo + preposición fija (comply with, refrain from, adhere to)
branches.example: Participants must **refrain from** smoking.

branches.if: Una duración hasta un punto futuro
branches.example: By 2030, the museum **will have been operating** for a century.

branches.if: Un plan oficial o una orden
branches.example: The monument **is to be** restored next year.

branches.use: be on the verge / brink of + -ing o sustantivo
branches.example: The language **is on the verge of** extinction.
The report **is due to** be published on Monday.

branches.use: be set to / be bound to
branches.example: Prices **are set to** rise again.

C2-10-0.title: Del plan neutro al anuncio oficial

steps.label: Neutro
steps.sentence: They**'re going to** demolish the old station.

steps.label: Oficial
steps.sentence: The old station **is to be** demolished.
steps.change: Be to: anuncio oficial, típico de la prensa.

steps.label: Programado
steps.sentence: Demolition **is due to** begin in June.

steps.label: Inminente
steps.sentence: The building **is on the verge of** collapse.

steps.label: Duración futura
steps.sentence: By June, campaigners **will have been fighting** for ten years.

items.a: By 2030, I **will have lived** here for twenty years.
items.b: By 2030, I **will have been living** here for twenty years.
items.note: Casi iguales; el continuo destaca la experiencia y la duración.
Are to: instrucción oficial, casi una orden. Should: consejo.

items.a: The train **is due to** arrive at five.
items.note: Due to + infinitivo, o due + hora sin infinitivo: las dos son correctas.

items.a: The species **is on the verge of** extinction.
items.b: The species **is on the verge to** become extinct.
items.note: On the verge of + sustantivo o -ing: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.example: The sequel is every bit as good as the original.
Prices are marginally higher than last year.
Life is considerably slower in the village.
The city is far more expensive now.
Today's buildings are nowhere near as solid as the old ones.

branches.example: **The older** I get, **the more** I value tradition.

branches.if: Igualdad enfática (contra lo que se cree)
branches.use: every bit as / just as… as
branches.example: Oral history is **every bit as** valuable **as** written records.

branches.use: nowhere near as / not nearly as
branches.example: The remake is **nowhere near as** moving **as** the original.

branches.use: not so much X as Y
branches.example: It's **not so much** nostalgia **as** grief.
Cities are getting **bigger and bigger**.

items.note: No better than: igual de malo (crítica). Not better than: simplemente no es mejor.
As many as con contables (sorpresa por la cifra); as much as, con incontables o dinero.
Con superlativo se usa by far: la segunda es incorrecta.

items.a: **The more** you learn, **the less** you know.
items.note: Cada mitad necesita the: la segunda es incorrecta.

C2-10-2.title: Proverbios sobre el tiempo y el cambio

items.en: Time and tide wait for no man.
items.es: El tiempo no espera a nadie.

items.en: Rome wasn't built in a day.
items.es: No se ganó Zamora en una hora.

items.en: Every cloud has a silver lining.
items.es: No hay mal que por bien no venga.

items.en: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
items.es: No vendas la piel del oso antes de cazarlo.
Obras son amores, que no buenas razones.

items.en: Where there's a will, there's a way.

items.word: at the end of the day
items.example: At the end of the day, it's your call.
items.es: al fin y al cabo (cliché oral)

items.example: I lost the job, but every cloud…
Sooner or later, the building will need repairs.
By and large, the reforms have worked.
Risk is part and parcel of innovation.
First and foremost, we must protect the archive.

items.b: Well, **every cloud has a silver lining**.
items.note: Los nativos suelen recortar el proverbio: basta con la primera mitad.

items.b: **At the end of the day**, the policy succeeded.
items.note: En un ensayo, by and large es aceptable; at the end of the day suena a cliché oral.
La expresión es fija: time and again (una y otra vez) o from time to time (de vez en cuando).

items.a: Change is **part and parcel** of life.
items.b: Change is **part and package** of life.
items.note: Las expresiones fijas no admiten cambios de palabra: la segunda es incorrecta.
